paper_metadata.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
paper_metadata.abstract: State-of-the-art computer vision systems are trained to predict a fixed set of predetermined object categories. This restricted form of supervision limits their generality and usability since additional labeled data is needed to specify any other visual concept. Learning directly from raw text about images is a promising alternative which leverages a much broader source of supervision. We demonstrate that the simple pre-training task of predicting which caption goes with which image is an efficient and scalable way to learn SOTA image representations from scratch on a dataset of 400 million (image, text) pairs collected from the internet. After pre-training, natural language is used to reference learned visual concepts (or describe new ones) enabling zero-shot transfer of the model to downstream tasks. We study the performance of this approach by benchmarking on over 30 different existing computer vision datasets, spanning tasks such as OCR, action recognition in videos, geo-localization, and many types of fine-grained object classification. The model transfers non-trivially to most tasks and is often competitive with a fully supervised baseline without the need for any dataset specific training. For instance, we match the accuracy of the original ResNet-50 on ImageNet zero-shot without needing to use any of the 1.28 million training examples it was trained on. We release our code and pre-trained model weights at https://github.com/OpenAI/CLIP.

extraction_data.innovation: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP): trains a dual-encoder model to predict which image-caption pairs are correct by maximizing agreement between image and text representations, enabling zero-shot transfer to downstream vision tasks without task-specific training; differs from prior supervised vision models by using natural language supervision instead of manual labels.
extraction_data.pretraining_corpus: 400M (image, text) pairs from the web (including Wikipedia articles, WordNet synsets)
extraction_data.finetuning_task: Supervised discriminative fine-tuning / linear probing, Linear probe (logistic regression classifier on frozen features)
extraction_data.research_problem: Learning transferable visual representations from natural language supervision
extraction_data.application: Zero-shot image classification, OCR, action recognition in videos, geo-localization, fine-grained object classification
extraction_data.paper_title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
extraction_data.finetuning_data: ImageNet, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, Oxford-IIIT Pet, Food-101, Stanford Cars, FGVC Aircraft, DTD, EuroSAT, RESISC45, Country-211, Stanford Dogs, PCam, VGG Flower, Kornblith et al. 12 datasets, GTSRB, Country211, SUN397, Kinetics700, UCF101, PatchCamelyon, CLEVR-Counts, SST2, Hateful Memes, FER2013, Food101, SUN09, Caltech-101, STL-10, Oxford-IIIT Pets, SUN, Flowers-102, Birdsnap, Kinetics-700, PASCAL VOC 2007, MNIST, ImageNet-Vid
extraction_data.attention_mechanism: Multi-head self-attention (ViT and Text Transformer); attention pooling mechanism for ResNet, Multi-head self-attention (Transformer) for text; Patch-based self-attention (ViT) or convolutional (ResNet) for images, Multi-head self-attention (ViT), Convolution (ResNet), Multi-head self-attention
extraction_data.training_pipeline: Joint training of image and text encoders on WIT dataset using contrastive loss
extraction_data.fusion_architecture: Late fusion (separate encoders with cosine similarity)
extraction_data.vision_encoder: Image encoder (CNN/Transformer unspecified), ResNet or Vision Transformer (ViT)
extraction_data.base_model: Trained from scratch without ImageNet or pre-trained weights
extraction_data.benchmark_result: Matches the accuracy of the original ResNet-50 on ImageNet zero-shot without needing to use any of the 1.28 million training examples it was trained on; competitive with a fully supervised baseline on over 30 datasets (OCR, action recognition, geo-localization, fine-grained classification);
